items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 16, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: something that I recorded with Clifford Jordan and Vernel Fournier.

ctx.x: Two days. It was Kobe Jazz Festival. And it was all done in eight hours those two days, because we did this from 12-4, three concerts a day. Like 12 to 12:40, 2 to 2:40 or something like that. You know by 4 o’clock you’re finished. anyway this was very successful for me because I don’t get a chance to go out of the country by myself that much, just by myself, just on my own merit. I’m usually with somebody else who has a name. I think there are some places where if I went by myself nobody would show up because…

they are they’re not around really playing anymore. So that’s my purpose for releasing these things more so than a hit album. I doubt if I’ll ever — I’ve given up on the idea of becoming a popular star. I don’t think I ever wanted that man, because I like my private life. And consequently I’ve done my own booking and so forth because if I want to go and visit my kids and my granddaughter, I don’t want anybody telling me but I booked this and you’ve got to go and do that. So consequently I guess I’ve got 50…

items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 16, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I found me and most of my friends, Vernell Fournier, we all grew up together.

ctx.x: You’ve been able to take your practical experience as a player and channel it into an educational delivery to the public schools?

For 35 years. I’ve done — or maybe 40 — I’ve done what’s called a lecture- demonstration. I think Billy Taylor started this in the 60s, where we lecture and we demonstrate. And I’ve been doing that constantly, every year, because for me it’s been like a commitment. Naturally education — I’ve done all these Broadway shows and Count Basie and all of that, and I realized that education is the key to it. Because when I first started playing trombone, I think maybe last time I told you when I was 12 years old I played…

items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I played drums in grammar school, along with Vernel Fournier

ctx.x: We want to ask you some things about jazz, about some things maybe that young people don’t know today, and see if you can fill us in and tell us some things in your career that guided you along the way, and some aspects, I also want to talk about some aspects of oral culture. How old were you when you first started playing?

I played drums in grammar school, along with Vernel Fournier, who is with Ahmad Jamal’s group. I imagine I was about eight or nine when I first started playing drums. And this was just little parade drums.
What attracted you to the music? What drew you into a musical career?
